seoTitle: Keep Table Rows From Splitting Across Pages in Docs
metaDescription: Stop table rows from breaking across pages in Google Docs by disabling row overflow in Table Properties and using Keep with next for related text.
intro: A table row that splits awkwardly across two pages looks unprofessional in a data-heavy report. This guide covers accessing the Table Properties panel to disable row overflow, using the Keep with next paragraph setting for related text, and adjusting cell padding so your tables stay cleanly contained on a single page.

steps.heading: Select your table
steps.body: Click into the table you want to fix and locate the primary formatting parameters in your document workspace.

steps.heading: Open Table Properties
steps.body: Right-click the table and choose Table Properties to launch the advanced sidebar configuration dashboard.

steps.heading: Navigate to Row settings
steps.body: Open the Row dropdown segment to reveal the automated cell separation restrictions for your table.

steps.heading: Disable row overflow
steps.body: Uncheck Allow row to overflow across pages to force a secure structural page-break boundary around each row.

steps.heading: Apply Keep with next for related text
steps.body: Use the Keep with next paragraph constraint to lock individual text fields to their subsequent data blocks.

steps.heading: Adjust padding and row height
steps.body: Fine-tune cell padding and row height to prevent premature page breaks or awkward white spaces around your data.

faq.question: Why does my table row keep splitting even after formatting changes?
faq.answer: Check that Allow row to overflow across pages is unchecked in Table Properties, since this setting is the main cause of rows splitting across pages.

faq.question: Does disabling row overflow work for every row automatically?
faq.answer: The setting applies at the table level, so it affects all rows within that table once configured.

faq.question: Can I keep a caption with its table using a similar setting?
faq.answer: Yes, applying Keep with next to the paragraph directly above or below the table helps lock captions to their related data block.

faq.question: Will this setting affect how my table prints?
faq.answer: Yes, it ensures the same clean row boundaries apply consistently whether you're viewing on screen or printing the physical document.
